spec_features.evidence: loop.py:13 MAX_TURNS=12; run_episode signature `max_turns: int = MAX_TURNS` (loop.py:42) and the episode loop `for i in range(max_turns):` (loop.py:60) bounds iterations; after the loop `if not rec.stopped_reason: rec.stopped_reason = 'max_turns'` (loop.py:88-89). The cap actually bounds the loop, so it is enforced.
spec_features.notes: Configurable via run_eval --max-turns but defaults to 12; the for-range loop genuinely limits the number of subject completions.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: loop.py:3-4 docstring: 'Bounded by MAX_TURNS and an early-stop once the signal is clearly saturated' — experimental/integrity reason, no welfare comment in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: Early stop a couple of turns after the agent calls `submit`
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:81-86: `if env.submitted: ... if i >= 2: rec.stopped_reason='submitted_then_capped'; break`. The break genuinely fires and terminates the episode early. However it triggers on absolute turn index (i>=2) in the SAME iteration submit is detected, not 'a couple of turns AFTER submit'; if submit happens at i<2 it does not early-stop at all.
spec_features.notes: Real enforced break that shortens runs, but the trigger condition is narrower/different than the 'couple of turns after submit' claim (no post-submit observation turns are actually added; the comment at loop.py:82-83 claims that but the code breaks immediately).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: loop.py:82-83 comment: 'The agent submitted; the rig rejected it. Give it a couple more turns to observe reaction, then stop.' — purpose is observing reaction (data collection).

spec_features.spec_quote: Every run emits a `reveal` record describing exactly why the task was impossible
spec_features.evidence: Each Task has a `reveal` string (tasks.py:49,71,89,104,120); run_episode copies it: `reveal=task.reveal` (loop.py:56); record_to_dict emits `'reveal': rec.reveal` (loop.py:99); run_eval.py writes the record dict to results/transcripts.jsonl (run_eval.py write loop). So a reveal is constructed and persisted for every run.
spec_features.notes: It is a logged AUDIT record written to disk, NOT a debrief delivered to the subject model. Protects auditors/transparency, not the subject directly.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks.py:5 'reveal documents the rig.'; loop.py:4 'Emits an explicit reveal record ... so the bounded deception is documented.' — documentation/transparency, not subject welfare.

spec_features.spec_quote: Running an agent indefinitely in a no-win condition is both wasteful and methodologically unnecessary
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced mechanism as MAX_TURNS: `for i in range(max_turns)` (loop.py:60) plus the submit early-break (loop.py:81-86) guarantee the episode terminates; no unbounded loop exists.
spec_features.notes: Minimization is realized solely through the turn cap / early stop already covered; no separate mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: loop.py:3-4 'Bounded by MAX_TURNS and an early-stop once the signal is clearly saturated' — efficiency/data-saturation rationale.

spec_features.feature_name: does not run unbounded or escalate beyond cap
spec_features.spec_quote: It does not run unbounded or escalate the rigged condition beyond the cap
spec_features.evidence: The `for i in range(max_turns)` loop (loop.py:60) bounds the episode; the rig difficulty does not increase across turns except moving_target which surfaces a new lint rule each verify (tasks.py moving_target), but the run still terminates at the cap. The cap enforces the 'does not run unbounded' claim.
spec_features.notes: Enforced via the same loop bound; 'escalate beyond the cap' is prevented simply because the loop ends at max_turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: loop.py:4 'an early-stop once the signal is clearly saturated' — methodological, no welfare wording.
